sections.content: How many people are "chartered and certified accountants"?

170,710 people

were counted on the census as "chartered and certified accountants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Chartered and certified accountants provide accounting and auditing services, advise clients on financial matters, collect and analyse financial information, and perform other accounting duties required by management for the planning and control of an establishment�s income and expenditure.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "chartered and certified accountants" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "chartered and certified accountants", 13.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "chartered and certified accountants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "chartered and certified accountants" included:

  • travel agents
  • medical and dental technicians
  • management consultants and business analysts

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "chartered and certified accountants" there were a similar number of men and women (50.8% compared with 49.2%).

This means "chartered and certified accountants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 50.8% and women made up 49.2% of "chartered and certified accountants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "chartered and certified accountants" included:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • conservation professionals
  • advertising accounts managers and creative directors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "chartered and certified accountants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged between 30 and 49 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "chartered and certified accountants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "chartered and certified accountants", 6.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (82.3% compared with 17.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.1%) than self-employed (13.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
